entry.title: Sutra on the Path of the Ten Wholesome Deeds
entry.summary: The Buddha teaches the dragon king how ten wholesome paths of bodily, verbal, and mental conduct support Buddhist practice. Chinese translation credited to Śikṣānanda in the Tang period.

entry.title: Sutra on the Eight Realizations of Great Beings
entry.summary: Eight reflections on impermanence, desire, diligence, wisdom, generosity, and compassion guide the path of awakening. Chinese translation traditionally credited to An Shigao in the Later Han period.

entry.title: Sutra of the Buddha's Bequeathed Teaching
entry.summary: The Buddha's final instructions on discipline, contentment, diligence, meditation, and wisdom before entering nirvana. Chinese translation credited to Kumārajīva in the Later Qin period.

entry.title: Essentials of Mind Transmission by Chan Master Huangbo Duanji
entry.summary: Huangbo's recorded teachings present the one mind and challenge attempts to seek awakening through attachment to concepts or external objects.

entry.title: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen
entry.summary: The collection preserves Yunmen's sermons, brief sayings, and exchanges with students on the realization and expression of Chan.

entry.title: Record of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou
entry.summary: Linji's recorded sermons and encounters urge direct realization and examine the student's dependence on names, roles, and borrowed understanding.

entry.title: Ritual for Mental Recitation of the Lotus Family in the Vajraśekhara
entry.summary: The manual sets out Lotus Family practice through visualization, mudrās, offerings, and mantra recitation within the Vajraśekhara ritual system.

entry.title: Explanation of the Secret Mind-Ground Method of the Great Yoga of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra
entry.summary: Amoghavajra explains the doctrinal and ritual framework of the Vajraśekhara teaching, including its maṇḍalas and stages of realization.

entry.title: The Diamond Scalpel
entry.summary: Zhanran argues that buddha-nature extends to insentient phenomena and examines objections to this Tiantai position.

entry.title: Profound Meaning of the Golden Light Sūtra
entry.summary: Zhiyi interprets the title and doctrinal structure of the Golden Light Sūtra through groups of three Tiantai principles.

entry.title: Explanation of the Gradual Method of the Perfection of Meditation
entry.summary: Zhiyi describes preparatory disciplines and successive meditative practices within the gradual approach to calming and contemplation.

entry.title: Record of Master Zhaozhou
entry.summary: Zhaozhou's recorded dialogues and sayings examine practice and awakening through exchanges with monastics and other visitors.

entry.title: Annotated Contemplation of the Huayan Realm of Reality
entry.summary: Zongmi annotates the contemplation text associated with Dushun, explaining its progression from emptiness to the mutual inclusion of phenomena.

entry.title: Profound Meaning of Guanyin
entry.summary: Zhiyi explains Guanyin through Tiantai categories, relating the bodhisattva's name and salvific activity to contemplation.

entry.title: Commentary on the Sublime Teaching of the Contemplation Sūtra
entry.summary: Zhili explains a commentary on the Contemplation Sūtra through Tiantai accounts of mind and the contemplation of the Buddha.

entry.title: Method of Contemplating Amitābha's Ocean of Marks and the Merits of Samādhi
entry.summary: Shandao explains the contemplation and recollection of Amitābha, supported by scriptural passages on practice and its benefits.

entry.title: Book of Serenity
entry.summary: Wansong comments on a collection of Chan cases and Hongzhi's verses, adding introductions, remarks, and explanations.

entry.title: Commentary on the Practices and Vows Chapter of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra
entry.summary: Chengguan explains the practices and vows of Samantabhadra and their place in the bodhisattva path.

entry.title: Record of Exploring the Profound Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra
entry.summary: Fazang comments on the sixty-fascicle Avataṃsaka Sūtra and elaborates Huayan doctrine through its sequence of assemblies and teachings.

entry.title: Profound Mirror of the Huayan Realm of Reality
entry.summary: Chengguan comments on the contemplation of the realm of reality associated with Dushun, explaining emptiness and the unobstructed relation of principle and phenomena.

entry.title: Calming and Contemplation in the Five Huayan Teachings
entry.summary: The work organizes contemplation into five teachings, moving from elementary analysis toward the interpenetration of all phenomena.

entry.title: Ten Mysterious Gates of the One Vehicle of Huayan
entry.summary: The work explains ten ways in which phenomena interpenetrate within the Huayan understanding of the one vehicle.

entry.title: Commentary on the Meaning of the Bodhisattva Precepts
entry.summary: Zhiyi explains the bodhisattva precepts of the Brahmā's Net Sūtra, relating ethical observance to the Mahāyāna path.

entry.title: Record of Chan Master Dongshan Wuben of Junzhou
entry.summary: The collection records Dongshan's teachings, encounters, and verses, including the Song of the Jewel-Mirror Samādhi.

entry.title: Encouragement to Advance through the Chan Gate
entry.summary: Zhuhong collects accounts and admonitions concerning sustained Chan practice, emphasizing resolve, effort, and the investigation of awakening.

entry.title: General Preface to the Collected Explanations of the Source of Chan
entry.summary: Zongmi compares Chan approaches and Buddhist doctrinal teachings, explaining their relation through awakening and cultivation.

entry.title: Yongjia's Collection on Chan
entry.summary: Xuanjue discusses preparation for practice, calming and contemplation, and the relation of understanding to realization.

entry.title: Treatise on the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life
entry.summary: Vasubandhu describes aspiration for birth in Amitābha's land through verses and an explanation of five gates of contemplative practice.

entry.title: Commentary on the Verses of Aspiration for Birth
entry.summary: Tanluan comments on Vasubandhu's Pure Land treatise, explaining the five gates of practice and the role of Amitābha's vows.

entry.title: Treatise on Birth and Nonbirth in the Pure Land
entry.summary: Chuandeng explains how aspiration for birth in the Pure Land accords with the nonarising of phenomena in Tiantai thought.

entry.title: Ten Essentials of the Pure Land
entry.summary: The anthology brings together Pure Land writings selected by Zhixu in a version abridged and annotated by Chengshi.

entry.title: Meaning of the Lotus Sūtra's Practice of Ease and Joy
entry.summary: Huisi explains practices associated with the Lotus Sūtra, including contemplation, endurance, and the cultivation of ease and joy.

entry.title: Collected Explanations of Restraint in the Vinaya
entry.summary: Duti collects explanations of the rules governing restraint, bringing Vinaya sources and commentaries together for practical study.

entry.title: Further Explanation of Required Acts in the Vinaya
entry.summary: Duti expands on Daoxuan's collection of monastic procedures, explaining the acts and communal observances required by the Vinaya.

entry.title: Commentary on Great Calming and Contemplation
entry.summary: Zhanran comments on Zhiyi's Great Calming and Contemplation, explaining its structure, contemplative methods, and doctrinal foundations.

entry.title: Commentary on the Bodhisattva Precepts of the Brahmā's Net Sūtra
entry.summary: Fazang comments on the bodhisattva precepts, examining their wording, classifications, and conditions of observance and transgression.

entry.title: Instructions for Newly Ordained Monks on Conduct and Vinaya Observance
entry.summary: Daoxuan sets out guidance for newly ordained monks on daily conduct, communal life, and the observance of monastic discipline.

entry.title: Essentials of Doctrine and Contemplation
entry.summary: Zhixu presents a concise account of Tiantai classification and connects each teaching with its corresponding contemplative practice.

entry.title: Ritual of Offerings and Recitation for Entering the Lotus Womb Maṇḍala of Mahāvairocana
entry.summary: The ritual manual describes entry into the Womb Realm maṇḍala through preparation, offerings, visualization, mudrās, and recitation.

entry.title: Treatise on the Jewel-King Samādhi of Buddha Recollection
entry.summary: Feixi discusses buddha recollection and samādhi, relating devotional practice to contemplative insight and the bodhisattva path.

entry.title: Record of Chan Master Chewu
entry.summary: Chewu's recorded instructions relate the recollection of Amitābha to faith, aspiration, and sustained Pure Land practice.

entry.title: Verses Praising Birth in the Pure Land
entry.summary: Shandao arranges verses, invocations, and acts of worship for devotion to Amitābha and aspiration for birth in the Pure Land.

entry.title: Record of the Source-Mirror
entry.summary: Yanshou assembles scriptural passages, treatise excerpts, and discussions to explain the one mind and relate Chan realization to Buddhist doctrine.

entry.title: Collection on Peace and Bliss
entry.summary: Daochuo distinguishes the path of sages from the Pure Land path and explains aspiration and practices for birth in Amitābha's land.

entry.title: Outline of the Four Teachings of Tiantai
entry.summary: Diguan summarizes the five periods and eight teachings, with an outline of the four doctrinal teachings and their stages of practice.

entry.title: Extensive Ritual Manual of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra
entry.summary: The manual organizes practices associated with the Mahāvairocana Sūtra, including maṇḍala rites, offerings, and mantra recitation.

entry.title: Commentary on the Sequence of Offerings in the Mahāvairocana Sūtra
entry.summary: Bukesiyi explains the sequence of offering practices associated with the Mahāvairocana Sūtra, including preparation, visualization, and ritual acts.

entry.title: Commentary on the Mahāvairocana Sūtra
entry.summary: Yixing records explanations of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra, treating its doctrine, maṇḍala, initiations, and ritual practices.

entry.title: Explanation of the Meaning of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra
entry.summary: This recension of the Mahāvairocana commentary explains the sūtra's teachings and ritual system in fourteen fascicles.

entry.title: Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra
entry.summary: Chengguan provides a detailed commentary on the eighty-fascicle Avataṃsaka Sūtra, explaining its chapters and Huayan accounts of the realm of reality.

entry.title: Mind-Only and the Middle Way: Yogācāra and Madhyamaka in China
entry.summary: Read Kumārajīva, Jizang, Xuanzang and Kuiji through the Three Treatises, the Thirty Verses, and the hundred dharmas.

entry.title: The Vinaya in China: Monastic Discipline and the Dharmaguptaka Rule
entry.summary: Explore the Four-Part Vinaya, Daoxuan’s work on Mount Zhongnan, and the bodhisattva precepts of the Brahmā’s Net Sutra.

entry.title: Tiantai and Huayan: Two Great Systems of Chinese Buddhist Thought
entry.summary: Meet Zhiyi, Fazang and Zongmi through calming and insight, the golden lion, and Chinese Buddhism’s teachings on an interconnected world.

entry.title: Pure Land Buddhism: Amitābha, the Three Sutras and the Practice of Recollection
entry.summary: Read the three Pure Land sutras and meet Huiyuan, Tanluan, Daochuo, and Shandao through Amitābha's vows and the practice of recollection.

entry.title: Chan Buddhism: From Bodhidharma to the Platform Sutra and the Lamp Records
entry.summary: Meet the early Chan teachers, read the Dunhuang Platform Sutra, and follow the five houses through the Record of the Transmission of the Lamp.

entry.title: Esoteric Buddhism in Tang Chang'an: Amoghavajra, Huiguo and the Road to Kūkai
entry.summary: Meet the teachers of Tang esoteric Buddhism and explore their scriptures, from Amoghavajra’s Chang’an to Huiguo’s transmission to Kūkai.

entry.title: The Heart Sutra: Text, Translators and How to Read It
entry.summary: Explore the Heart Sutra through Xuanzang's Chinese text, its Sanskrit mantra, and a gentle passage-by-passage introduction to wisdom and emptiness.

entry.title: The Eight Schools of Chinese Buddhism
entry.summary: Explore eight Buddhist traditions through their great teachers, foundational texts, and a practical first reading for each school.

entry.title: Start Here: Reading the Chinese Buddhist Canon
entry.summary: Find your first Buddhist text, learn how the Chinese canon is arranged, and build a reading practice with sutras, teachers, and commentaries.
